from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Lorentz Oscillator Model", [
            "Electrons are bound to the nucleus like springs.", 
            "Light waves shake these electrons periodically.", 
            "The oscillating electron radiates its own field."
        ])
        
        # Setup elements
        nucleus = Dot(color=BLUE).scale(2)
        spring = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, color=GREY)
        electron = Dot(color="#FF0000").scale(1.5)
        electron.next_to(spring.get_end(), RIGHT)
        
        model = VGroup(nucleus, spring, electron)
        self.place_at_grid(model, 'C2', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(model))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(wave, 'C4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(wave))
        
        # Oscillation
        self.play(electron.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(electron.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(electron.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        dipole = Arrow(electron.get_center(), electron.get_center() + UP, color="#FFFF00")
        self.add(dipole)
        self.play(GrowArrow(dipole))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Origin of Refractive Index (n)", [

            "Effective wave speed decreases in the medium.",
            "Dipole interference slows the wave significantly."

        self.wait(1)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        retardation_label = Text("Phase Velocity Retardation", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")

class SineWave(VMobject):
    def __init__(self, x_range, amplitude, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.set_points_smoothly([np.array([x, amplitude * np.sin(3*x), 0]) for x in np.linspace(x_range[0], x_range[1], 50)])

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Different colors have different refractive indices.",
            "Snell's Law dictates unique bending angles.",
            "Prisms split white light into rainbows."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Dispersion: The Prism", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        c1 = "#FFFFE0" # Light Yellow
        c2 = "#AFEEEE" # Pale Turquoise
        c3 = "#FFD1DC" # Pastel Pink

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(c1))
        
        # Display prism geometry
        prism = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2, UP*2, color="#ADD8E6", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(prism, "D3")
        self.play(Create(prism))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(c2))
        
        # Incoming light
        white_beam = Line(LEFT*2, ORIGIN, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        white_beam.move_to(self.grid["D2"])
        self.play(Create(white_beam))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(c3))
        
        # Split beams
        red_beam = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2 + UP*0.5, color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        blue_beam = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2 - UP*0.5, color=BLUE, stroke_width=4)
        
        red_beam.move_to(self.grid["D4"])
        blue_beam.move_to(self.grid["D4"])
        
        self.play(Create(red_beam), Create(blue_beam))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Real-world Application", [
            "Color dependence is inherent to matter.", 
            "Chromatic aberration affects lens performance.", 
            "Achromatic doublets cancel chromatic dispersion."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show refractive index formula summary #FFFFFF.
        formula = MathTex(r"n(\omega) \approx 1 + \sum \frac{f_j \omega_p^2}{\omega_j^2 - \omega^2}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display lens refracting light rays #00FF00.
        lens = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(lens, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        ray1 = Line(start=np.array([-2, 1, 0]), end=np.array([0, 1, 0]), color=RED)
        ray2 = Line(start=np.array([-2, 0.5, 0]), end=np.array([0, 0.5, 0]), color=BLUE)
        
        self.play(Create(lens), Create(ray1), Create(ray2))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight real-world optical glass application #FFD700.
        doublet = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=1.0, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3),
            Circle(radius=1.0, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3).shift(RIGHT * 0.5)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(doublet, "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(doublet))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Origin and Color Dependence of the Index of Refraction

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Lorentz Oscillator Model
sections.content: Briefly introduce electrons in a material as 'bound' to the nucleus by a spring-like force. When an electromagnetic wave (light) strikes, the electron oscillates, creating a secondary dipole field. The phase difference between the driving wave and the electron's response determines the refractive index.
sections.example: Visualize an electron as a mass on a spring; light is the rhythmic shaking of the support base.

sections.title: The Origin of Refractive Index (n)
sections.content: Explain that the index of refraction n = c/v. Since the electron's dipole radiation interferes with the original light wave, the resulting 'effective' wave travels slower. Mathematically, n is related to the polarizability of the medium (n² ≈ 1 + χ).
sections.example: A hiker (light) walking through a dense forest (medium) with many 'bouncy' obstacles (electrons) that cause the hiker to adjust speed.

sections.title: Color Dependence (Dispersion)
sections.content: Introduce the resonance frequency (ω₀). As the frequency of light (ω) approaches the natural frequency of the electrons (ω₀), the electron's amplitude and phase delay shift drastically. This creates 'normal dispersion', where n increases with frequency (blue light bends more than red).
sections.example: Use a graphical animation of a playground swing: pushing at low frequency vs. pushing at resonance frequency changes how the swing moves.

sections.title: Visualizing Dispersion: The Prism
sections.content: Connect the microscopic physics to macroscopic observation. Because different colors have different indices of refraction in glass, they bend at different angles (Snell's Law: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂).
sections.example: Show a classic triangular prism splitting white light into a rainbow, labeling the paths of blue vs. red light clearly.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-world Application
sections.content: Summarize that color dependence is an inevitable consequence of light-matter interaction. Mention Chromatic Aberration in high-end camera lenses as a critical engineering challenge resulting from this principle.
sections.example: An 'Achromatic Doublet' lens system used in a telescope, where two different glass types are combined to cancel out the color-bending effects.
